text: @my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status 是 DSH Web 插件，在消息输入框工具栏提供 MCP 连接面板。它读取配置的 MCP server 行，展示连接阶段、目标位置和已注册工具数，并通过开关按需挂载或卸载 MCP client；读取列表本身不会改变连接。可用于只在需要时启动常用配置之外的 MCP 服务，并查看本次运行的连接状态。插件重启后由面板管理的连接不会保留；需要 DSH Web profile 和已有 MCP server 配置。

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status adds an MCP panel to the DSH Web toolbar. It lists configured servers, connection states and tool counts, and lets users connect or disconnect servers on demand. Status reads do not alter connections; panel-managed connections last for this run. Requires configured MCP rows.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status 的功能「查看 MCP 状态」：工具栏面板列出配置的服务器、目标和连接阶段，并显示每个服务器注册的工具数。打开或刷新列表只读取状态，不会发起连接。
@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status 的功能「按需连接和断开」：用户切换服务器开关时，插件挂载对应 MCP client 或释放挂载。连接结果会区分已连接、连接中和失败等状态。
@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status 的功能「连接等待上限」：连接操作默认最多等待 8000 毫秒后向面板报告仍在连接；可选 connectTimeoutMs 配置限制在 0 到 120000 毫秒。
@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status 的功能「兼容启用中的配置行」：如果 profile 中某个 MCP 行仍启用，关闭面板开关会经 Plugin Manager 将该行设为禁用；面板自己打开的连接则只在本次运行中管理。
@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status 使用前须知：现有 MCP 行需禁用才能避免启动时连接；关闭仍启用的行会将禁用状态写回 profile。（见 index.js:363-366）

[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的 MCP 连接面板插件。

它在对话输入框下方的工具栏里加一个按钮，列出本机所有 MCP 服务器，并逐个开关连接。
**不存任何东西：每次启动都是全关**，你手动开这一轮要用的那几个。关掉 DSH 就全断，
下次启动重新从零开始。

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · 为什么需要它：DSH 里每个 MCP 服务器都是一行 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`。这些行一旦启用，Loader
在启动时就会逐个拉起连接；连不上时 supervisor 进入重连退避（500ms → 30s，最多 10 次），
于是后台每几十秒就重试一次。对不常用的服务器来说，这既拖慢启动，也一直在烧子进程和
连接尝试。

本插件把「要不要连」这件事从启动时挪到用户手上：行保留为纯配置，连接由面板按需建立，
而且**只在本次运行内有效**——不存在「上次开着的这次自动连上」这种事。
@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · 从 GitHub 直装：dsh plugin --profile web add github:my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · 界面：- 按钮只显示 `MCP 2/3`（已连接数/总数），左侧圆点表示是否有连接（有连接=绿色，读取失败=红色）。
- 点开是一个 **320px 面板**，列表按「已连接 / 未连接」**分组**：打开的第一眼就能看到谁在
  跑，不必逐行读状态。分组标题右侧是这一组的条数。
- 每行 44px：状态点、服务器名、一行元信息、工具数、开关。**工具数单独占一列**（右对齐、
  等宽数字），因为它是「这条连接真的通到了东西」的唯一证据；没工具时显示 `—`。
- 元信息只放**能区分这台服务器的那一点**（URL 的 host、脚本名或传输方式），完整命令行
  在 `title` 里悬停可见，不在 320px 里挤成一坨截断的碎片。
- 字号已按可读性下限校准：服务器名 13px、其余正文与标签 12px（原本有 10px/11px 的）。
- 面板打开时每 4 秒刷新一次；关闭时不发请求。刷新只是读状态，**不会动任何连接**。
- 尺寸与相邻 chip 一致：高 28px、`radius-sm`、13px/20px、同样的 hover 底色。
- 亮色与暗色都只用 DSH 主题令牌，切主题不会花；正文对比度实测 ≥5.6:1。
- 中英文案跟随界面语言。

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · 它是怎么工作的：**行是纯配置。** 每个 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 行继续作为服务器配置的唯一来源
（transport / command / args / env / url），但被置为 `disabled: true`，Loader 不再挂载它们，
所以启动时零连接、零重连计时器。

**不存任何东西。** 开着的服务器集合只活在这个插件实例的内存里。重启、重载插件、改 profile，
都会让集合清空——**每次启动都是零连接**，你要用哪个就开哪个。

这条是刻意的。MCP 服务器一旦连上就是常驻子进程 + 一条长连接，还要占着 `serverName`（同一个
名字同一时刻只能有一个活着的实例）。把「上次开着的这次自动连上」做出来，等于把启动期的连接
成本又搬回来了，只是换了个人决定。所以这里干脆不记：**只有你在这一轮里亲手打开的东西才连**。

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · 它是怎么工作的：**连接由面板接管。** 打开开关时，插件用该行的配置在自己的 context 里挂载官方
`dsh-mcp-client` 插件，工具与资源照旧注册到 `ctx.tools`；关闭开关时 dispose 掉挂载，传输关闭、
工具注销。**面板不写 profile**：开关是运行时动作，不是配置编辑，所以它不会改你的
`cordis.patch.yml`，也不会触发重新组合插件树。

**读列表不会重连。** 面板的 `list` 路由是纯投影：它报告每一行此刻的 phase、工具数和开关状态，
不做任何连接动作。**只有开关操作**会真的挂载或卸载——这是关键，否则第二个窗口、第二个会话
每读一次列表就把别人正在用的连接拆掉一次（早期按工作区协调的版本正是这样，表现为工具在
会话中途反复「新增/移除」，甚至调用时报 `unknown tool`）。

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Host 路由：两条都在需要认证的 `/api` 通道上，客户端用同源 `fetch('api/...')` 调用。

- `GET api/mcp-status.list` → `{ servers: [{ entryId, serverName, transport, target, enabled,
  connected, phase, tools, managedBy, editable }] }`
- `POST api/mcp-status.set` `{ entryId, enabled }` → `{ ok, application, status }`；
  连不上时 `{ ok: false, reason: 'connect-failed', diagnostic }`

两条都不需要 `sessionId`：面板没有「按会话」的语义，读也只是一次投影。

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Why this plugin：In DSH each MCP server is one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row. While such a row is enabled, the Loader opens its connection at startup; a server that fails to connect sends the supervisor into reconnect backoff (500ms → 30s, up to 10 attempts), so the background keeps retrying every few dozen seconds. For servers you rarely use that both slows startup and keeps burning child processes and connection attempts.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Why this plugin：This plugin moves the "should this be connected?" decision from startup to the user: rows stay as pure configuration, connections are opened on demand by the panel, and **they last only for this run** — nothing you opened last time comes back on its own.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · The interface：It sits in the toolbar row below the composer: the same flex container (`.tools`) as the "+" button and the permission chip ("工作区内修改"), immediately to the right of that chip.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · The interface：- The button reads `MCP 2/3` (connected / total); the dot on its left shows whether anything is connected (green = connected, red = the read failed).
- Clicking opens a **320px panel whose list is grouped by state** — connected and not connected. Opening it answers "what is running" before a single row's status is read; each group heading carries its own count.
- Each 44px row holds a status dot, the server name, one line of metadata, the tool count, and a switch. **The tool count gets its own column** (right-aligned, tabular figures) because it is the only proof the connection actually reached something; with no tools it reads `—`.
- The metadata line carries only what **distinguishes this server** (the URL's host, the script name, or the transport); the full command line is available on hover via `title`, rather than being truncated into fragments at 320px.
- Type sizes are calibrated to the readability floor: server names at 13px, all other body and label text at 12px (several were 10px/11px).
- While open the panel refreshes every 4 seconds; while closed it issues no requests.
- It matches the neighbouring chip: 28px tall, `radius-s

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · The interface：The design record is kept in `spec.md`, `directions.md`, and `direction-approved.md`, with the
three directions and their screenshots under `design-demos/` (`thumbs.html` for the six
candidates, `dir-1/2/3.html` for the three full directions, `index.html` for the side-by-side
comparison). The shipped version is direction C: grouped by connection state rather than sorted
by name.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · How it works：**Rows are pure configuration.** Each `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row remains the single source of truth for a server's settings (transport / command / args / env / url), but it is set to `disabled: true` so the Loader mounts none of them. Startup therefore opens zero connections and runs zero reconnect timers.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · How it works：**Nothing is stored.** The set of open connections lives in this plugin instance's memory only. A restart, a plugin reload or a profile edit empties it — **every start is zero connections**, and you open whichever server this run needs.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · How it works：That is deliberate. A connected MCP server is a long-lived child process plus a live connection, and it holds a `serverName` (only one live instance per name). Persisting the set would put the startup connection cost right back where it came from, just with a different decider. So this panel keeps no record: **only what you opened in this run is connected.**

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · How it works：**The panel owns connections.** Switching a server on mounts the shipped `dsh-mcp-client` plugin in this plugin's own context with that row's config, so its tools and resources register into `ctx.tools` exactly as before; switching it off disposes the mount, closing the transport and unregistering the tools. **The panel does not write the profile**: a switch is a runtime action, not a configuration edit, so it never rewrites `cordis.patch.yml` or recomposes the tree.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · How it works：**Reading never reconnects.** The `list` route is a pure projection: it reports each row's current phase, tool count and switch, and performs no connection work. **Only a switch operation** mounts or unmounts anything. That matters: an earlier build reconciled per workspace on every read, so a second window or Session polling the list tore down a connection another one was using — visible as tools being added to and removed from a running Session, and as `unknown tool` failures mid-conversation.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · How it works：**One compatibility path.** If a row is still enabled in the profile, the panel reports it honestly as "connected (maintained by that row)". Switching it off persists `disabled: true` through the Plugin Manager, which is the only place the panel ever writes configuration — and only when you explicitly turn such a row off.
@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Host routes：Neither takes a `sessionId`: the panel has no per-Session semantics, and a read is just a projection.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Configuration：The row in `cordis.patch.yml` accepts an optional config, overridable through the user patch layer:

```yaml
- id: mcp-status
  name: '@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status'
  config:
    # Milliseconds to wait for one connection (default 8000). After the bound

There is no database and no state to clean up. Upgrading from a build that had
one, the old `$DSH_HOME/mcp-status/mcp-status.db` is simply no longer read and
can be deleted:

```sh
rm -rf ~/.dsh/mcp-status
```

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Dependencies：Nothing third-party is imported at runtime: the MCP plugin is fetched through `ctx.loader.import('@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client')`, so this bundle declares no `dependencies`. The Host half imports nothing at all — no filesystem, no SQLite.

The client half is plain JavaScript (`React.createElement`, no build step) and requires only `react` and `react-dom` from the platform module table.

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Source layout：```
dsh-mcp-status/
├── index.js            # Host half: MCP rows, mount/unmount, two /api routes (no persistence)
├── client.js           # Client half: the toolbar button and its panel
├── cordis.patch.yml    # Bundle patch: inserts the mcp-status row

@my-dsh/dsh-mcp-status README · Publishing：Publishing this package to npm requires an npm account that can write to the `@my-dsh` scope. `package.json` already sets `publishConfig.access: public`, so a maintainer runs:

```sh
npm login                       # needs the @my-dsh-scope account
npm publish
```

The repo-root `.npmrc` pins the registry to `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, so a publishing machine needs no manual registry switch. `npm pack --dry-run` previews the exact tarball.
